Alpha Centauri A.description: Primary of the Alpha Centauri system; a Sol-like star and the anchor of human space.

Alpha Centauri B.description: Orange companion to Alpha Centauri A; its industrial worlds orbit under a dimmer, redder sky.

Alpha Centauri C.description: The red dwarf Proxima; it dominates Proxima's night sky though it lies far from the A–B pair.

Regulus A.description: Fast-rotating blue subgiant at the heart of the Regulus system; Tycho's fierce daylight comes from this star.

Delta Pavonis.description: Quiet G-type subgiant; La Bella Vista orbits under warm, steady light.

61 Virginis.description: Sol-like star hosting Irasia's heavy industry and trade lanes.

61 Ursae Majoris.description: Stable main-sequence star anchoring Tokirev's cold industrial orbit.

18 Scorpii.description: Near-Solar analogue; Fennet grew under its calm temperate light.

Tau Ceti.description: Quiet G dwarf; Fortuna's finance districts orbit a dimmer, steadier sol.

61 Cygni A.description: Orange dwarf of the 61 Cygni binary; New Carthage trades under its ruddy light.

Epsilon Eridani.description: Young K dwarf with elevated particle wind; Horizon's vast cities orbit here.

Wolf 359.description: Dim flare star; Titania IX rides the turbulent skies of its gas-giant primary nearby.

Kepler-16 A.description: Primary of the Kepler-16 circumbinary; Pelagos sees two sols from its sky.

Sirius A.description: Brightest star in Old Earth's night sky; its white light is a familiar marker in the inner systems.

Sirius B.description: Dense white-dwarf companion to Sirius A, a remnant of a once more massive star.

Procyon A.description: Yellow-white subgiant in the Procyon binary, brighter and hotter than the Sol.

Procyon B.description: Compact white-dwarf companion orbiting Procyon A.

Barnard's Star.description: Red dwarf famous for its large proper motion across the Old Earth sky.

Lalande 21185.description: Red dwarf in Ursa Major and one of the closest stellar neighbors to Sol.

Ross 154.description: Active Red dwarf in Sagittarius, known for energetic flares.

Lacaille 9352.description: Red dwarf with a comparatively bright apparent presence for its class.

Kapteyn's Star.description: Old high-velocity red dwarf whose motion marks it as a member of the Galactic halo population.

Groombridge 34 A.description: Red dwarf in a binary system, with a companion separated by a wide orbit.

Luyten's Star.description: Red dwarf in Canis Minor with a long history of astrometric study.

Wolf 1061.description: Red dwarf known to host a compact planetary system.

GJ 15 A.description: Red dwarf in a binary system with a low-mass stellar companion.

YZ Ceti.description: Active red dwarf with a compact planetary system.

LHS 1140.description: Cool red dwarf known for hosting a temperate exoplanet.

TRAPPIST-1.description: Ultra-cool red dwarf famous for its compact system of seven Old Earth-sized planets.

GJ 436.description: Red dwarf hosting a well-studied warm gas giant.

GJ 3470.description: Red dwarf with a low-density Neptune-sized planet.

Epsilon Indi A.description: Orange dwarf in a multiple system, surrounded by a faint stellar and substellar entourage.

Epsilon Indi Ba.description: Brown-dwarf companion to Epsilon Indi A; its spectrum is dominated by molecular absorption.

Epsilon Indi Bb.description: Cooler brown-dwarf companion in the Epsilon Indi system.

61 Cygni B.description: Cooler companion of 61 Cygni A, with deep orange-red light.

40 Eridani A.description: Orange main-sequence primary of a hierarchical triple system.

40 Eridani B.description: White-dwarf companion in the 40 Eridani triple system.

40 Eridani C.description: Red-dwarf outer companion of the 40 Eridani system.

Struve 2398 A.description: Nearby flare-star primary in a binary red-dwarf system.

GJ 887.description: Red dwarf with a relatively high surface temperature for an M star.

GJ 667 C.description: Red-dwarf component of a triple system with several reported planetary signals.

GJ 486.description: Red dwarf hosting a short-period terrestrial planet.

GJ 1214.description: Cool Red dwarf hosting a well-studied small gas giant.

Ross 128.description: Quiet Red dwarf with a known Old Earth-sized planetary companion.

Gliese 876.description: Red dwarf whose planetary system includes multiple giant planets in compact orbits.

Gliese 832.description: Red dwarf with a long-period planetary companion.

Gliese 581.description: Red dwarf made famous by early reports of multiple low-mass planets.

Gliese 667 A.description: K-type primary in the Gliese 667 triple system.

Gliese 667 B.description: Cooler stellar companion to Gliese 667 A.

HD 40307.description: Orange dwarf known for a compact family of detected planets.

HD 85512.description: Orange dwarf with a well-studied planetary candidate from early radial-velocity surveys.

HD 20794.description: Sol-like star with a long history of precision radial-velocity observations.

HD 69830.description: Orange dwarf with a prominent debris disk and several detected planets.

HD 10180.description: Sol-like star with a rich planetary system originally inferred from precision radial velocities.

HD 189733 A.description: Orange dwarf hosting the intensely studied hot gas giant HD 189733 b.

HD 209458.description: Sol-like star hosting one of the first exoplanets observed transiting its star.

51 Pegasi.description: Sol-like star whose hot gas giant companion helped launch the ancient era of exoplanet discovery.

55 Cancri A.description: G-type primary hosting a notably diverse multi-planet system.

47 Ursae Majoris.description: Sol-like star with a long-studied system of giant planets.

Upsilon Andromedae A.description: F-type star with a historically important multi-planet system.

Kepler-16 B.description: Low-mass companion that makes the Kepler-16 system a true binary-star planetary environment.

Kepler-90.description: Sol-like star known for a remarkably large planetary system.

Kepler-11.description: Sol-like star hosting several tightly packed transiting planets.

Kepler-62.description: Cooler orange star with a compact system including two planets in its habitable-zone region.

Kepler-186.description: Red dwarf hosting five known planets, including an Old Earth-sized planet in the temperate zone.

Kepler-452.description: Sol-like star with a well aged planetary system and a well-known transiting rocky super planet.

Kepler-1649.description: Cool red dwarf hosting an Old Earth-sized planet receiving a temperate level of stellar radiation.

Kepler-22.description: Sol-like star with an early-discovered transiting planet in its habitable zone.

TOI-700.description: Cool red dwarf with a compact planetary system containing Earth-sized worlds.

TOI-715.description: Cool red dwarf hosting a transiting planet near the inner edge of its temperate zone.

LHS 475.description: Red dwarf with an Old Earth-sized transiting planet.

LP 791-18.description: Cool red dwarf with a compact planetary system containing a volcanically interesting terrestrial world.

GJ 357.description: Red dwarf with a compact planetary system.

GJ 1132.description: Cool red dwarf whose rocky planet is a target for atmospheric studies.

GJ 9827.description: Orange dwarf hosting several small transiting planets.

K2-18.description: Cool red dwarf hosting a small gas giant in a temperate orbit.

WASP-12.description: Hot, slightly evolved F-type star hosting an extremely irradiated giant planet.

WASP-17.description: Hot F-type star hosting a highly inflated gas giant.

WASP-39.description: Sol-like star whose transiting gas giant has been a major target for atmospheric spectroscopy.

WASP-96.description: Sol-like star hosting a hot gas giant with a well-observed atmosphere.

WASP-121.description: Hot F-type star orbited by an ultra-hot gas giant.

55 Cnc B.description: Faint stellar companion to the 55 Cancri planetary system.

Sol.description: The Old Earth's G-type primary and the historical reference point for human stellar measurements.

Vega.description: Rapidly rotating A-type star and a historic photometric standard, surrounded by a bright debris disk.

Altair.description: Rapidly rotating nearby A-type star whose flattened shape reflects its high spin rate.

Fomalhaut A.description: A-type star encircled by a prominent debris disk.

Arcturus.description: Orange giant and one of the brightest stars visible from Old Earth.

Aldebaran.description: Orange giant marking the eye of Taurus, with a surface far cooler than the Sol.

Betelgeuse.description: Red supergiant in Orion, nearing the end of its stellar evolution.

Rigel.description: Blue supergiant in Orion radiating with enormous luminosity.

Deneb.description: Luminous blue-white supergiant marking the tail of Cygnus.

Antares A.description: Red supergiant at the heart of Scorpius, with a hot blue companion nearby.

Canopus.description: Bright white-yellow supergiant-like giant and the second-brightest star in Old Earth's night sky.

Achernar.description: Rapidly rotating blue star with a strongly oblate shape.

Spica A.description: Hot blue primary in the close Spica binary, a major navigation beacon in Virgo.

Spica B.description: Hot blue companion to Spica A in a tight stellar orbit.

Pollux.description: Orange giant in Gemini and one of the closest evolved stars to Sol.

Castor A.description: White A-type component of the Castor multiple-star system.

Castor B.description: Second bright A-type component of the Castor multiple system.

Capella Aa.description: Cool giant component of the close Capella binary.

Capella Ab.description: Hotter giant companion orbiting Capella Aa.

Polaris Aa.description: Cepheid variable and the primary of the Polaris multiple system.

Regulus B.description: Cool companion to the rapidly rotating Regulus A.

Bellatrix.description: Hot blue giant marking Orion's shoulder.

Alnilam.description: Extremely luminous blue supergiant at the center of Orion's Belt.

Alnitak.description: Hot massive multiple system forming the eastern star of Orion's Belt.

Mintaka A.description: Hot blue primary of the Mintaka multiple system in Orion's Belt.

Mimosa.description: Hot blue giant marking one of the principal points of the Southern Cross.

Hadar A.description: Massive blue giant in a multiple system and a prominent southern-sky star.

Acrux A.description: Hot blue component of the Acrux multiple system at the foot of the Southern Cross.

Shaula.description: Hot blue star in Scorpius, with a close stellar companion.

Alkaid.description: Blue main-sequence star at the end of the Big Dipper's handle.

Mizar A.description: Bright A-type component of the famous visual multiple system in Ursa Major.

Mizar B.description: Companion to Mizar A, forming a celebrated double-star pair.

Alcor.description: A-type companion visually paired with Mizar in Ursa Major.

Eta Carinae A.description: Extremely luminous unstable massive star surrounded by the Homunculus Nebula.

R Doradus.description: Cool red giant with one of the largest stellar disks.

Mira A.description: Pulsating red giant and prototype of the long-period Mira variable stars.

Algol A.description: Hot primary of the eclipsing Algol system, whose brightness changes reveal its orbital geometry.

Algol B.description: Cooler evolved companion of Algol A in the famous eclipsing binary.

Sadr.description: Yellow-white supergiant near the center of the Northern Cross.
